It added one new tower, and quite a few important patch notes. NEW TOWERS Pursuit - Unlocked from reaching Level 100, Pursuit was the second aerial-based tower after the Ace Pilot, so it was completely immune to stuns. It would circle around the path, but unlike the Ace Pilot, it would stop circling to target an enemy in its range, it would only stop firing if all enemies were killed in its range, or if all enemies exited its range. This is a double-edged sword as the Pursuit was way more consistent than the Ace Pilot, but fast enemies often just walked right past it. It also had the same placement limit, being 10. Anyways, as for the stats, it was quite cheap for the DPS it dealt, though the DPS was hampered quite a lot by the ROF bug though. It can also deal splash damage at Level 2+, though the missiles have a mediocre damage and explosion radius, so they weren't really useful, but it does make the tower a better counter to shielded enemies, as it also fires fast. matches.title: Tierlist of all HC + Evo Towers
matches.snippet: Tierlist of all HC + Evo Towers 9. Brawler. Decent for speedrunning. That's all. 8. Necromancer. Very map and mode dependent, great for HC, VC and PW2, but pretty useless besides that. 7. Accelerator. Outclassed by every DPS tower except Turret and Pursuit. 6. Engineer. Jack Of All Trades, Master Of None. Struggles in early-game, mid-game and late-game, very support-unfriendly, was useful in LHC and LFM, but not in their modern versions. 5. Operator. Extremely good early, and holds up pretty well till the late game, but has alternatives like G Soldier, which can be even better. 4. Enforcer. Map and modes dependent (sucks in Frost, shines at Pizza Party and Fallen). Crazy damage and CE plus stuns, though short range. 3. Hacker. The only good HC tower. Multiple strong abilities, very versatile and useful, can increase your DPS drastically with it's clones and doesn't even need to be upgraded to level 5, but is very expensiive and loadout-dependent. 2. Juggernaut. Extremely good for mini/final boss/bosses and for overall damage on Bottom Path, and very strong support and Cost Efficient on Top Path + has hidden and flying/lead. Kingpin. Crazy DPS, strong eco, versatility, 2 detections + 1 semi-detection. Good practically everywhere.

Crook unit Health: 10 -> 25 Crook unit Damage: 2 -> 1 Crook unit Range: 13 -> 20 Golden Crook Boss now spawns “Golden Crook” which does 2 damage instead of 1 Level 5 Damage: 7 -> 9 (Golden: 9 -> 12) (Platinum: 8 -> 10) Mafia unit Health: 10 -> 50 Mafia unit Range: 15 -> 24 Golden Crook Boss now spawns “Golden Mafia” which does 5 damage instead of 2 This buff was absolutely massive, the tower was made cheaper while the overall DPS was increased. It became very strong in the early game. Base Crook Boss now pretty much had the strength of Golden Crook Boss before the buff, and Golden Crook Boss was absolutely insane now. Level 3 GCB dealt 23.33 DPS for only $2,875, which is one of the best cost-to-DPS ratios in the entire game. The minions being buffed was also nice. The setbacks of short range and 6 placement limit are still there. Base Crook Boss gets bumped up to B tier, while Golden Crook Boss gets bumped up to an outstanding S tier, now #3. Level 2, 3 and 4’s damage were increased from 2 to 3, while Level 5’s damage was increased from 5 to 6. Holiday Archer Level 0 Cost: $200 -> $350 This does affect its early levels quite a bit, making Level 0-2 look too weak for their cost, but remember, the tower still has infinite pierce with no damage fall-off. verified_top_matches.snippet: TDS Tower Ranking (Release v1.7) Part 19 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.7, it added one new tower, the Electroshocker, and a few quite minor patch notes. NEW TOWERS: Electroshocker - The Electroshocker is a support tower that chains a stun effect to multiple enemies at once. Its chain range even extends beyond its listed range, the range is already quite a lot for a support tower, so it is really effective at slowing down hordes.. The stun duration is short, and it has no hidden detection and a 2 placement limit, but overall, it offered more utility than the Pyromancer at the time, especially with fewer enemies being immune to it. Ranked on B tier. BALANCE CHANGES (Release v1.7) - February 11th, 2020 Enforcer Bullets now have damage dropoff as they pierce enemies. Level 0 Range: 9 -> 7 Level 1, 2, 3 Range: 11 -> 9 Level 4 Range: 12 -> 9 Level 5 Cost: $6,250 -> $7,500 Range: 13 -> 10 This change really doesn’t affect the tower that much, it’s still an all-rounder tower, and it still destroys crowds. It only drops a few placements below on the S tier. Scout/Golden Scout Level 3, 4 Range: 17 -> 16 Level 5 Range: 18 -> 17 Don’t really know what was the point of this nerf, but whatever.. Both towers stay at the same spot. Rocketeer Level 0 Damage: 6 -> 5

TOWER RANKING: F TIER #35 - Paintballer - Paintballer has horrible DPS for how expensive it is, bad range, and the explosion radius is so small that it may just be a single target tower. There’s almost no point in using it, the only thing it has going for it is auto hidden detection, but even then that’s a thing that almost every tower has. #34 - Gladiator - Gladiator’s DPS is decent enough for its cost, so it may seem like a good early game tower on paper, but the problem is its range is abysmal (because it’s a melee tower), AND the fact that it can miss its swings, so it’s pretty much deadweight against any enemy with above average or higher speed. It’s still not worth using, there are many other towers you can use for early game. D TIER #33 - Hunter: Hunter is not a terrible early game tower per chance at its lower levels, it also has decent range, but the problem is, upgrading it is not just not worth your money. #32 - Scout: Level 0 Scout is actually quite cost efficient and spammable for early game, its later upgrades except for Level 4-5 were pretty useless though. Level 4-5 Scouts can somewhat handle mid-game of the easier modes, but still gets easily overwhelmed. #31 - Demoman: Demoman may have splash damage, but the splash radius is small, and even then its DPS is pretty bad, it does get better at Level 5 but it’s still below average. #30 - Ace Pilot: Ace Pilot may have extremely good DPS for its cost, but the problem is that DPS is super inconsistent since the tower flies so slow and the attack range is also pretty bad. It requires good placement to even do anything, and that’s not even mentioning its placement limit of FIVE. The tower was just not worth using. #29 - Commando: Commando was extremely cost inefficient across all levels, has no hidden detection, but if you somehow have the enough money to spam Level 5 Commandos, it's surprisingly decent for late game combined with its missiles. C TIER #28 - Farm: Farm does a decent job at giving cash, and can make you rich really quick by spamming Farms since they have no placement limit. However, most of the time, you don't really need it for cash. Simply dealing damage was just enough. #27 - Soldier: Soldier was surprisingly effective at Levels 0 and 1, being cheap and spammable for early game. However, upgrading it past that was pretty much pointless and a waste of money. #26 - Medic: Medic can heal the base health, but that ability is just useless. Its DPS is alright, and it is surprisingly quite cost efficient at Level 2 and 3. Level 5's Cleansing ability to remove stuns and debuffs is honestly quite useful, and that's really there is going for it. #25 - Sniper: Sniper was strong in the early game thanks to its enormous range and decent starting DPS. Unfortunately, people don't really use him to his full potential and he has a bit of a curve as to how to use him, so it'll eventually get complicated. 5 - Accelerator - ONE Nerf and everybody thinks this guy's garbage. He's still a top 5 DPS tower, and a genuine monster when you need him to be. Every strat that takes juggernaut will also work just as well with Accelerator, and hes the most beginner friendly choice for your first gem/hardcore tower. Don't let anyone tell you accelerator is bad. 6 - Enforcer - Okay. Enforcer. Guy's pretty good, but there really isn't much to say about him. He has no identity beyond going from "Guy with a Shotgun" to "Guy with a Stronger Shotgun" and a Swat van. He gains some extra points for the Swag factor, but hes... Really Alright? 7 - Engineer - It's the Age Old Gambit Here; Jack of all Trades, Master of None. Engineer underperforms in Early Game, Underperforms in Midgame, having all detections does not save her, she's only good on later levels, and her only saving graces are not only the fact she's good supporting DPS, also the fact that the other towers on this list are just that much worse than she is. 8 - Necromancer - TDS's Potential Man. Necro is map dependant, requires alot of mental gymnastics to justify his existence, and is overall not worth the grind. You can squeeze the most use out of him if you actively micro him though, but other than that he's in a really bad position. 9 - Brawler - I hate to put this guy here but genuinely, no tower is in worse position than Brawler. verified_top_matches.snippet: Tierlist of all HC + Evo Towers 9. Brawler. Decent for speedrunning. That's all. 8. Necromancer. Very map and mode dependent, great for HC, VC and PW2, but pretty useless besides that. 7. Accelerator. Outclassed by every DPS tower except Turret and Pursuit. 6. Engineer. Jack Of All Trades, Master Of None. Struggles in early-game, mid-game and late-game, very support-unfriendly, was useful in LHC and LFM, but not in their modern versions. 5. Operator. Extremely good early, and holds up pretty well till the late game, but has alternatives like G Soldier, which can be even better. 4. Enforcer. Map and modes dependent (sucks in Frost, shines at Pizza Party and Fallen). Crazy damage and CE plus stuns, though short range. 3. Hacker. The only good HC tower. Multiple strong abilities, very versatile and useful, can increase your DPS drastically with it's clones and doesn't even need to be upgraded to level 5, but is very expensiive and loadout-dependent. 2. Juggernaut. Extremely good for mini/final boss/bosses and for overall damage on Bottom Path, and very strong support and Cost Efficient on Top Path + has hidden and flying/lead. Kingpin. Crazy DPS, strong eco, versatility, 2 detections + 1 semi-detection. Good practically everywhere.
